newsitem.title: UK: Love of Eurolire to bloom with more rate cuts seen.
newsitem.headline: Love of Eurolire to bloom with more rate cuts seen.

text.p: Investors' lust for Eurolire will continue amid expectations of further interest rate cuts before the year-end, new issues traders said on Thursday.
"The Eurolira market is the most euphoric in Europe at the moment," Credito Italiano syndicate manager in Milan said.
"All Eurolira players are happy this morning," he added.
The Bank of Italy cut the key discount rate to 7.50 percent from 8.25 percent on Wednesday night -- seen as a sign the country believes it has a grip on inflation.

A further chop of up to 75 basis points was expected before the end of 1996, although some conservative estimates see room for only a 25 b.p. shave, if inflation dips firmly below three percent in November.
"The cut has given some breath to the economy, which was slowing down too much," J.P. Morgan's head of lira-spread product Luigi Moroni said.
"Another 75 basis point cut before the end of the year is expected," he added.

Eurolira traders said there would now be a short-term bout of profit-taking leading to a mild correction, but investors were likely to use this to jump back into the market as soon as bonds started to offer good value.
"This is still a market to buy," Moroni said.

The Euromarket has seen a flow of lira-denominated bonds in the past two months driven by expectations of Italy joining European economic and monetary union (EMU) and the resulting European interest-rate convergence.
The zero-coupon sector in particular has seen a flood of new issues.

"There's been huge retail appetite for long-dated zero- coupon bonds as the supranationals like the World Bank and the EBRD are exempt from inheritance tax," a Citibank Eurolira syndicate official in London said.
"But the accounts for this paper are now full so we don't expect much more zero-coupon paper."
The 10-year sector has seen strong attraction with spreads tightening, traders said. Others said the best window from a technical point of view was in the five-year area.
"Spreads are constantly tightening and people are switching from the five- into the 10-year sector as there is a 50 basis point pick-up from five to 10 years," a trader said.
Credit Local, DSL Bank and the European Investment Bank have all recently tapped the 10-year Eurolira sector. Primary market traders said they expected more German banks to follow.
But some cautioned that funding levels for triple-A financial institutions were quite tight so it would be difficult to match their funding requirements with an acceptable spread.
Others said corporates would borrow in the fixed-rate sector in the three-, five- and seven-year area.
"Investors are now looking to extend their maturities," J.P. Morgan's Moroni said, adding heavy demand was seen from Italian retail investors as well as from Germany and Luxembourg.
They were attracted by the high coupons lira paper offers.

"Italian retail investors are tapping the sector, 70 to 80 percent of all Eurolira issues are sold into Italy as it is a very cash-rich country...Even if lira has softened a bit, the cash BTP market is still holding well," Moroni said.
This morning, Credit Local de France added 100 billion lire to its 8.125 percent 10-year bond at an issue price of 101.79.
"The market is going very well and the evidence is that this morning we increased the Credit Local deal," the Credito Italiano syndicate official said.
"It's bullish because the market expects Italy to enter EMU in the first round," he added.
